findings.title: Session identity can patch every pod in its namespace
findings.what: The dispatch Role grants get and patch on pods without resourceNames. Every workload using the bound dispatch ServiceAccount can therefore mutate labels and annotations on unrelated pods throughout the namespace. A compromised credential-bearing sidecar could interfere with selectors, policy controls, admission-driven behavior, or other pod-metadata consumers beyond its own session. The inline comment acknowledges that this is namespace-wide and defers confinement to future multi-tenant work, so the exposure is present in this baseline rather than speculative.
findings.fix: Remove namespace-wide pod patch permission. Have the trusted controller apply the claimed label, or create a per-session Role and RoleBinding after the generated pod name is known, with resourceNames containing only that pod.
findings.acceptance: Render the RBAC and verify with Kubernetes authorization checks that the dispatch ServiceAccount cannot patch an unrelated pod, while the trusted controller or per-session identity can still set probaitio.com/claimed=true on the intended session pod.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read probaitio-operator/config/rbac/dispatch_role.yaml:17-23 at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The rule still has resources [pods], verbs [get, patch], and no resourceNames restriction; its own comment explicitly confirms namespace-wide scope. The adjacent Secret rule remains independently restricted to resourceNames [claude-oauth].
